2.t: By the ten nights (i.e. the first ten days of the month of Dhul-Hijjah)

2.fn: Narrated Ibn ‘Abbâs رضي الله عنهما: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said, "No good deeds done on other days are superior to those done on these (first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah)." Then some Companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said, "Not even Jihâd ?" He replied, "Not even Jihâd, except that of a man who does it by putting himself and his property in danger (for Allâh’s sake) and does not return with any of those things." (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Vol.2, Hadith No.86).

3.t: And by the even and the odd (of all the creations of Allâh).

3.fn: "Even" and "Odd" is interpreted differently by different religious scholars. Some say: Even is the Day of Slaughtering of the Sacrifices, i.e. 10th of Dhul-Hijjah, and Odd is the Day of ‘Arafah (Hajj ), i.e. 9th of Dhul-Hijjah. Others say: Even is all the creatures and Odd is Allâh. Some say it is the compulsory congregational prayer, i.e. Maghrib is Witr , and the other four prayers are Shaf‘

4.t: And by the night when it departs.

5.t: There is indeed in them (the above oaths) sufficient proofs for men of understanding (and that, they should avoid all kinds of sins and disbeliefs)!

6.t: Saw you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) not how your Lord dealt with ‘Âd (people)

7.t: Of Iram (who were very tall) like (lofty) pillars,

8.t: The like of which were not created in the land?

9.t: And (with) Thamûd (people), who hewed out rocks in the valley (to make dwellings)?

9.fn: "And you hew out in the mountains, houses with great skill." [The Qur’ân, Verse 26:149].

10.t: And (with) Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) who had the stakes (to torture men by binding them to the stakes)?

11.t: Who did transgress beyond bounds in the lands (in the disobedience of Allâh).

13.t: So your Lord poured on them different kinds of severe torment.

14.t: Verily, your Lord is Ever Watchful (over them).

15.t: As for man, when his Lord tries him by giving him honour and bounties, then he says (in exultation): "My Lord has honoured me."

16.t: But when He tries him by straitening his means of life, he says: "My Lord has humiliated me!"

17.t: Nay! But you treat not the orphans with kindness and generosity (i.e. you neither treat them well, nor give them their exact right of inheritance)!

18.t: And urge not one another on the feeding of Al-Miskîn (the poor)!

19.t: And you devour the inheritance all with greed.

20.t: And you love wealth with much love.

21.t: Nay! When the earth is ground to powder.

22.t: And your Lord comes with the angels in rows.

23.t: And Hell will be brought near that Day. On that Day will man remember, but how will that remembrance (then) avail him?

24.t: He will say: "Alas! Would that I had sent forth (good deeds) for (this) my life!"

25.t: So on that Day none will punish as He will punish.

26.t: And none will bind (the wicked, disbelievers and polytheists) as He will bind.

27.t: (It will be said to the pious believers of Islamic Monotheism): "O (you) the one in (complete) rest and satisfaction!

28.t: "Come back to your Lord well-pleased (yourself) and well-pleasing (unto Him)!
